newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Lehman sees Asia undervalued.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Lehman sees Asia undervalued.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said Asian markets appear increasingly undervalued, except for Hong Kong, following the recent rally in U.S. treasuries.

In a report issued on Monday, Lehman Brothers senior strategist in Asia Abhijit Chakrabortti said his favourite market was Malaysia, based on the long bond's price momentum, relative values (equity yield relative to risk adjusted benchmark interest rate) and earnings momentum.
For Thailand and India, however, Lehman has lowered its targets.
"While we remain overweight in both markets, the principal reason for lowering these targets is delayed recoveries in earnings," Chakrabortti said.
"Both markets are forecast to have some recovery in earnings in 1997, but we have lowered our expectations regarding the extent of those recoveries."
Within Hong Kong, the preference is for the property sector over the financial sector, the report said.

The property sector is expected to have positive earnings surprises as the sector benefits from historically low mortgage rates, consequently increased affordability and strong price rises in the residential segment.
Banks, however, may disappoint due to margin contraction and sluggish fee income growth, Chakrabortti said.

He said that the relationship between Hong Kong forward returns and Lehman Brothers long bond price momentum indicators suggests that the market in general, in particular the financial sector, already have a benign interest rate outlook priced in.
